## Summary

- ATAC peaks on the element centre. H3K27ac peaks on the flanking nucleosomes at +/-250 bp and is still at 28% of maximum at +/-2 kb, past the models' ~1.1 kb receptive field (Fig. 2).
- +/-500 bp is the widest counting window with no other element's centre inside it. Widening to +/-2000 bp raises the replicate ceiling on the top quintile (the 20% of elements with the most H3K27ac signal) only from 0.760 to 0.798 (Fig. 3).
- At 1 bp a perfect model of H3K27ac shape reaches only *r* = 0.21 (K562) and 0.18 (GM12878) on the top quintile, and 0.72 and 0.70 at 50 bp bins (Fig. 4). Profile-head scores should be read against that cap.
- Accessibility explains H3K27ac best in K562 (top-quintile *r* 0.51 against 0.33-0.41 elsewhere), and the ordering changes when all elements are scored (Fig. 1). So every evaluation is stratified, and coupling is measured in each new cell type before training.
- K562 ATAC has a clean nucleosomal ladder, with a sub-nucleosomal mode at 42 bp and a mono-nucleosomal peak near 205 bp, so fragment-size channels can be built (Fig. 5).

## Goals

This report describes the H3K27ac and ATAC data and what is predictable from them without a model, including every ceiling in the project. See also Report 2 (evaluation methodology), Report 3 (design decisions: each architecture and input change tried, and its verdict) and `reference/DATA_INVENTORY.md` (every assay across the nine cell types, including files that must not be used).

## Accessibility explains less of H3K27ac outside K562, and the ordering changes when all elements are scored

The ATAC-only model scores lower in GM12878 because accessibility and H3K27ac are less coupled there. Coupling, the model-free correlation of summed ATAC with summed H3K27ac per element, is the denominator that makes accessibility-based scores comparable across cell types. Relative to it, the model does better in GM12878 than in K562:

| | K562 | GM12878 |
|---|---|---|
| model-free ATAC-H3K27ac coupling | 0.510 | 0.409 |
| ATAC-only model | 0.542 | 0.467 |
| model / coupling | 1.06 | 1.14 |

Sequence-only falls 0.360 -> 0.146 with no such denominator to explain the drop. This sharpens the transfer conclusion: accessibility transfers, only sequence collapses.

> **Superseded (F-016, 2026-09-14):** Scored against the target cell type's own accessibility-only model trained on the same assay (the floor), no transferred sequence+accessibility H3K27ac model beats it in any of six directions, so transfer fails for the full model too.

## H3K27ac sits on flanking nucleosomes and is far broader than ATAC

ATAC peaks on the element centre (offset −12 bp, no central dip). H3K27ac has shoulders at +/-250 bp on the flanking nucleosomes and is still at 28% of its maximum at +/-2 kb, where ATAC has fallen to 17%. That is the edge of the profiled window, so H3K27ac extends further than measured here.

![](figures/profile_comparison.png)

<details>
<summary>Figure 2 legend</summary>

**Figure 2 | H3K27ac is displaced onto flanking nucleosomes and is much broader than accessibility.** Meta-profiles in 50 bp bins, top H3K27ac quintile (n = 30,000 elements, seed 0), all tracks on the same elements. **a**, Each track normalised to its own maximum. **b**, Raw magnitudes, log scale. Teal, K562 ATAC; orange, K562 H3K27ac 5' ends; dashed line, element centre. Peak offset −12.5 bp (ATAC) against −262.5 bp (H3K27ac); centre-to-peak ratio 1.000 against 0.944 (`results/profile_comparison_summary.tsv`). Source: `results/profile_comparison.tsv`.
</details>

<summary>Full methods &amp; code</summary>

## A 1 kb counting window is the best trade-off between signal and neighbour contamination

Count H3K27ac over +/-500 bp. Wider windows add little signal (top-quintile ceiling 0.760 at +/-500, 0.798 at +/-2000) and increasingly contain another element's centre (41.5% at +/-2000), whose reads cannot be attributed to the centred element. That matters for sequence attribution.

![](figures/fiveprime_h3k27ac_replicate_ceiling.png)

<details>
<summary>Figure 3 legend</summary>

**Figure 3 | The achievable ceiling saturates by +/-1 kb, while neighbour contamination keeps rising.** Pearson correlation of log H3K27ac counts between the two ENCSR000AKP replicates, by counting-window half-width, over all n = 150,526 candidate elements (teal) and the top quintile (purple). Replicate agreement bounds any model of the merged target. Top quintile: 0.729 (+/-250 bp), 0.760 (+/-500), 0.776 (+/-750), 0.785 (+/-1000), 0.795 (+/-1500), 0.798 (+/-2000). Elements with another element's centre in the window: 0% at +/-250 and +/-500 bp, 9.9% at +/-750, 19.9% at +/-1000, 33.1% at +/-1500, 41.5% at +/-2000 (`results/window_tradeoff.tsv`). Source: `results/fiveprime_replicate_ceiling_by_window.tsv`.
</details>

**Method.**

- Per-replicate 5'-end BigWigs built with the same processing as the merged training target.
- Neighbour contamination computed from element-centre spacing per chromosome.

<details>
<summary>Full methods &amp; code</summary>

Converting raw *r* to a bound on model performance is described in Methods.

Excluding the nucleosome-free centre lowers the top-quintile ceiling (excluding +/-125/+/-250/+/-375 bp: 0.760 -> 0.747 -> 0.729 -> 0.717), because the centre still carries ~94% of peak signal. Flanking-only counts correlate 0.93-0.99 with full-window counts, so the full window is kept (`results/flanking_vs_full_window.tsv`).

```bash
pixi run python scripts/0.3.replicate_ceiling_by_window.py \
    --elements reference/K562_DNase_candidate_elements.narrowPeak \
    --rep1-bw data/h3k27ac_rep1_5p_plus.bw,data/h3k27ac_rep1_5p_minus.bw \
    --rep2-bw data/h3k27ac_rep2_5p_plus.bw,data/h3k27ac_rep2_5p_minus.bw \
    --outdir results --figdir figures --label fiveprime_
pixi run python scripts/0.4.flanking_vs_full.py --outer 500 1000 --inner 0 125 250 375
```
Source: `scripts/0.3.replicate_ceiling_by_window.py`, `scripts/0.4.flanking_vs_full.py`
</details>

## H3K27ac has no reproducible base-resolution profile

At 1 bp a perfect model caps at *r* = 0.21 in K562 and 0.18 in GM12878 on the top quintile, so the base-resolution multinomial term of the loss is mostly fitting Poisson noise. The cap rises to 0.72 and 0.70 at 50 bp bins, and 0.79 and 0.78 at 100 bp.

![](figures/fig11_profile_ceiling.png)

<details>
<summary>Figure 4 legend</summary>

**Figure 4 | The reproducible part of the H3K27ac profile appears only after coarse binning.** Replicate-versus-replicate correlation across positions *within* each element, so only shape counts; 16,148 K562 and 15,589 GM12878 elements, +/-500 bp windows, strands summed. **a**, Raw agreement: 0.023 and 0.016 at 1 bp, top quintile. **b**, Ceiling on the pooled track the model is scored against, `sqrt(2r/(1+r))` (Methods). Solid, top quintile; dashed, all elements; dark, K562; light, GM12878. The curve is close to log-linear in bin size and still rising at 250 bp, so no bin size is preferred. There is no step near the ~180 bp nucleosome repeat, which indicates a broad envelope rather than sharply phased peaks. Source: `results/profile_ceiling_binsize_{k562,gm12878}.tsv`.
</details>

**Method.**

- Elements flat in either replicate are excluded; scoring them as 0 would mix "not reproducible" with "no shape to reproduce".
- 500 bp bins are omitted: a 1 kb window gives only 2 bins.

<details>
<summary>Full methods &amp; code</summary>

```bash
sbatch scripts/0.25.submit.sh
```
Source: `scripts/0.25.profile_ceiling_by_binsize.py`
</details>

## The ATAC library supports fragment-size stratification

K562 ATAC fragments form a clean nucleosomal ladder, but the two channels built so far capture only 50% of fragments. A four-channel input of [all fragments, sub, mono, di] would contain the current flat-accessibility input, so it cannot regress, and would add the higher-order peaks.

![](figures/atac_fragment_lengths.png)

<details>
<summary>Figure 5 legend</summary>

**Figure 5 | K562 ATAC fragment lengths show clear nucleosomal laddering.** Fragment-length density from TLEN of properly-paired reads, chr1, ~1.4 million fragments per replicate; the three ENCSR868FGK replicates (ENCFF077FBI, ENCFF128WZG, ENCFF534DCE) superimpose. Modes at 42 bp (sub-nucleosomal), ~205 bp (mono-), ~400 bp (di-) and ~600 bp (tri-); median 201 bp. Shaded: sub-nucleosomal channel 1-99 bp (30.3% of fragments) and mono-nucleosomal channel 180-247 bp (19.7%). **50.0% of fragments are in neither** (100-180 bp and above 247 bp, including both higher-order peaks). Source: `results/atac_fragment_length_summary.tsv`.
</details>

**Method.**

- Each properly-paired fragment counted once, via positive TLEN.
- Fragment lengths need the paired-end BAMs; the per-read Tn5 tagAlign files lose them.

<details>
<summary>Full methods &amp; code</summary>

```bash
pixi run python scripts/0.10.plot_fragment_lengths.py \
    --bams $SCRATCH/atac_pe/ENCFF077FBI.pe.bam $SCRATCH/atac_pe/ENCFF128WZG.pe.bam \
           $SCRATCH/atac_pe/ENCFF534DCE.pe.bam \
    --outdir results --figdir figures
```
Source: `scripts/0.10.plot_fragment_lengths.py`, `scripts/0.9.make_atac_fragment_channels.sh`
</details>

## DNase cut sites are reproducible at base resolution

By the method of Fig. 4, the 1 bp top-quintile ceiling is about four times higher for DNase than for H3K27ac:

| 1 bp, top quintile | DNase | H3K27ac |
|---|---|---|
| K562 | 0.848 | 0.21 |
| GM12878 | 0.686 | 0.18 |

K562 DNase reaches 0.921 at 5 bp and 0.946 at 10 bp, so predicting it at 5-10 bp loses almost nothing.

The downstream model reads accessibility as a base-resolution 5' insertion track, so an ATAC-to-DNase converter that predicted only per-element counts would strip the structure it uses. With a reproducible DNase profile to predict, the profile head becomes the decisive component of a converter, having been near-useless everywhere else in this project.

> **Superseded (F-014, 2026-09-13):** A converter that reproduced the DNase profile at 95% of its inter-replicate ceiling (F-011) still made a worse model input than plain ATAC in every direction tested, so predicting the profile well was not enough.

GM12878's DNase library is much weaker than K562's: top-quintile count ceiling *r* = **0.445** against 0.925 (+/-500 bp windows), 53.8M usable main-chromosome reads against 301.1M (5.6x), and 9.5% mitochondrial reads against 0.075%. The two ATAC libraries are matched (545.7M, 571.4M). DNase comparisons in GM12878 therefore confound assay with library quality, and cross-cell-type DNase comparisons confound it with depth. The K562 in-cell comparison is clean and conservative, because DNase is the *shallower* input there (301.1M against ATAC's 545.7M).

**Method.**

- Same script and procedure as the H3K27ac ceilings, so the numbers share one scale.
- Stranded per-replicate 5' tracks; read 1 only for paired BAMs, with pairing detected per file rather than from the metadata table.

<details>
<summary>Full methods &amp; code</summary>

K562's ENCSR000EOT is listed as pe + se, and a recorded constraint says mixed run types make an inter-replicate ceiling uncomputable (the reason HCT116's H3K27ac was excluded). 5' counting weakens that objection: one cut site per read, read 1 only for paired data, makes PE and SE libraries comparable at the cut-site level. The control, GM12878's ENCSR000EMT (two clean SE replicates), gives the same shape of curve, and K562's replicates agree *better* (0.562 at 1 bp, top quintile) than GM12878's (0.307). The mixed run type is not producing K562's result.

```bash
sbatch scripts/0.33.dnase_profile_ceiling.sh
```
Source: `scripts/0.33`, `scripts/0.25.profile_ceiling_by_binsize.py`,
`results/profile_ceiling_binsize_{k562,gm12878}_dnase.tsv`
</details>

## 5' insertion tracks remove a read-length confound that full-interval coverage carries

Full-interval coverage (`bedtools genomecov -bg` over the tagAlign interval) counts `read_length` bases per read, smearing each Tn5 insertion across ~95 bases in our K562 and GM12878 libraries. 5' insertion counts (`genomecov -bg -5`) count one base per read, so they compare across cell types sequenced at different read lengths. This is the ChromBPNet convention (`chrombpnet/helpers/preprocessing/reads_to_bigwig.py`: `-bg -5`, unstranded, ATAC shift `4-plus_shift, -4-minus_shift`). Our tagAligns are already Tn5-shifted, so the build only adds `-5`; shifting again would double-shift.

`sum(full-interval) / sum(5')` must equal the mean read length: 84.5 and 85.6 for K562 and GM12878 (94-95 bp reads), 30.9-35.5 for the four TeloHAEC conditions (35-36 bp). K562-versus-GM12878 comparisons were never affected, but TeloHAEC's full-interval coverage is a different quantity. With read length removed, the K562-versus-TeloHAEC gap falls from 13-27x to 5.3-12.3x nuclear depth, which is real sequencing depth. The effect of switching to 5' tracks on model performance is in Report 3.

## Element derivation differs between cell types, which is a standing confound

K562 and GM12878 candidate elements are DNase-derived; TeloHAEC's are ATAC-derived (`reference/ELEMENT_DERIVATION.md`). So the two cell types behind most results use elements from a different assay than their input. An ATAC-derived K562 set (`reference/K562_ATAC_candidate_elements.narrowPeak`, same rE2G model type as TeloHAEC's) makes this testable; the test is in Report 3. The ABC candidate regions for the downstream benchmark are ATAC-derived, from observed K562 ATAC.

## The training negative pool is not GC-matched, despite its filename

Training negatives are a uniform random sample of the genome, with mean GC **0.389** against **0.466-0.593** for candidate elements. Retraining on GC-matched negatives changes nothing measurable.

`reference/genomewide_gc_stride_1000_flank_size_1057.gc.bed` is ChromBPNet's GC-*annotated* genome tiling (3,088,298 bins, 1 kb stride, GC in column 4), the *input* to GC matching. Our training code reads only columns 1-3 and samples uniformly from a 50,000-window random subsample, using the same pool for K562 and GM12878.

- Negatives carry their true H3K27ac signal, not a hard zero, and are restricted to each fold's training chromosomes.
- No reported number is computed on them; evaluation uses candidate elements only (Report 2).
- GC-separable negatives can turn a BPNet-style sequence branch into a coarse GC detector (negatives are 10% of every batch, ~0.1 lower in mean GC), so this was tested as the cause of the flat sequence branch. GC-matched negatives give +0.001 in-cell type (*p*=0.76) and -0.002 transferred (*p*=0.33), with the match verified first: mean-GC gap closed 6.6x, largest per-bin discrepancy 5x (Report 3).

Nothing needs re-running. For new models, matched sets are `data/gc_negatives_{k562,gm12878}_h3k27ac.bed` (from `scripts/0.28`); the tiling keeps new numbers comparable with existing ones. The matching tool exits 0 having written nothing when `bedtools` is absent, and hangs when the foreground is GC-rich enough to exhaust the high-GC bins (repository learnings).

Separately, most candidate elements carry no H3K27ac, since the set spans active and inactive elements. That is why every evaluation is stratified.

## Methods

All ChIP-seq targets are counted as **5' read ends** at single-base resolution
(`bedtools genomecov -5 -dz`, stranded), matching the convention already used for the p300
models in this repository. Accessibility inputs exist in both conventions described above;
which one a given result used is recorded per result in `results/TARGET_PROVENANCE.md`.

Ceilings are reported as the raw inter-replicate *r*. Converting one to a bound on model
performance requires two corrections, applied wherever a fraction-of-ceiling is quoted
anywhere in this project: Spearman-Brown for the fact that the model predicts the
two-replicate *merge* rather than one replicate (`rel = 2r/(1+r)`), then a square root,
since a model predicts the expected signal while a replicate is one noisy realisation of it.
At +/-500 bp this converts a raw 0.760 into a bound of 0.929 on the top quintile, and a raw
0.844 into 0.957 over all elements.

Windows are centred on candidate-element midpoints rather than summits, because the H3K27ac
summit sits on a flanking nucleosome (Fig. 2). The `summit` column of
`K562_DNase_candidate_elements.narrowPeak` equals `width/2`, so element-centred windows
require no change to the extraction code. Elements within `flank` of a contig end are
dropped. Signal is read with pyBigWig and `nan` treated as zero.
